correctness.rationale: For fixed q>=2, alpha>-1 and sigma>0, the inspected radial angular-frequency blocks act on q-dimensional Jacobi polynomial subspaces for the Beta(xi+1,alpha+1) law. Under Y_xi=xi(1-t), every polynomial moment converges to Gamma(alpha+1), with positive limiting Hankel determinants and hence coefficientwise Jacobi-to-Laguerre orthonormal basis convergence. The symbol condition a(t)=c(1-t)^sigma+o((1-t)^sigma) plus boundedness gives a global power envelope, and higher fixed Beta moments yield uniform integrability. Thus xi^sigma M_xi converges in matrix norm to c times a positive-definite q-by-q Laguerre moment matrix. Finite negative-frequency blocks do not affect tails. Each of its q positive eigenvalue branches has xi^-sigma singular-value asymptotic; summing branch counting functions and inverting proves N^sigma s_N=|c|(sum_j nu_j^{1/sigma})^sigma in the limit. This yields compactness, p>1/sigma Schatten criterion and endpoint logarithmic coefficient. For sigma=1, Laguerre Jacobi trace q(q+alpha) gives the stated exact constant. Independently checked the q=2 alpha=1/2 sigma=1 matrix, trace, and positivity; numerical finite-block checks are not infinite proofs.
